scope: Original 2020 Dune: Imperium base game, standard 2–4 human players, including required two-player House Hagal. Solo-only p20, variants, expansions, promos and Uprising excluded.
verdict_explanation: One distinct source-defined outcome branch remains unrequired: ordinary untied Combat ranking and reward assignment. Existing questions extensively test ties and the two-player Rival but do not require the normal highest-strength/top-reward and second-highest/second-reward rule. No material answer-key error or edition/scope contamination was found.

findings.title: Untied Combat ranking and ordinary three-player reward cutoff are not required
findings.source_rule: During Resolve Combat, the highest-strength player wins and gains the top reward; the second-highest gains the second reward. An ordinary third-place reward is available only in a four-player game. Zero strength receives no reward.

existing_question_comparison.Q10: Tests Combat Intrigue eligibility/order/passing and win-trigger timing, but not which untied rank wins or which reward it gets.
existing_question_comparison.Q11: Its explicitly four-player scenario starts with a first-place tie, then asks other tie branches. C receiving third tests the residual four-player third reward, not ordinary first/second ranking. Its key contains no untied first/second allocation.
existing_question_comparison.Q20: Tests House Hagal combat strength, lack of Rival rewards, control removal, and human second-place ties. It does not require normal human first/second reward allocation.
existing_question_comparison.Q13: Tests the game winner and endgame tiebreakers, not Conflict reward ranking.

source_references.section: Resolve Combat and Ties; three-player worked example

proposed_additions.question: In a three-player Conflict, the three humans finish with 8, 6 and 4 strength, with no ties. Who wins, and which reward does each receive? What changes for an ordinary third-place finisher in a four-player game?
proposed_additions.fixed_answer: The player with 8 strength wins the Conflict and receives the top reward. The player with 6 receives the second reward. The player with 4 receives nothing in a three-player game. In a four-player game, an ordinary third-place finisher with positive strength receives the third reward. Zero strength never earns a reward.

source_references.section: Resolve Combat: highest, second-highest, third only in four-player; zero-strength exclusion

source_references.entry: Conflict: reward rules are the same for one, two and three players and differ for four

proposed_additions.novelty: Adds the ordinary untied resolution branch, not another arithmetic instance of the tie rules. A response could satisfy every existing required tie/Rival answer while never stating who wins an untied Conflict or that the second-highest player receives the second reward. The three-player cutoff is also not required by Q11’s four-player scenario. Four-player third place and zero-strength clauses are contextual reinforcement, not claimed as additional novelty.
proposed_additions.suggested_implementation: Either add this one item or explicitly extend Q11 to require ordinary untied first/second allocation and the three-player third-place cutoff. Do not count both implementations as separate new coverage.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Another deployment sum or different resource quantities
rejected_candidates.rationale: Q06/Q62 already require all new recruits plus at most two old garrison troops; changing quantities creates no rule branch.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Three or four humans tied for first, or another tie for second scenario
rejected_candidates.rationale: Q11 requires first/second/third tie rules generally; changing number of tied participants is a mechanical application. This differs from the accepted untied ranking branch.

rejected_candidates.candidate: A three-player second-place tie pays the third reward
rejected_candidates.rationale: Q11 already requires the general second-place tie rule and Q20 tests its survival without an ordinary third reward. Repeating it for three humans adds no distinct branch.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Staged Incident specifically requires moving the strength marker
rejected_candidates.rationale: Q09/Q10 already require recalculation and marker adjustment after Combat Intrigue changes strength. A named instance adds no independent outcome.

rejected_candidates.candidate: A moved Agent removes Hall of Oratory Persuasion or permits Maker spice
rejected_candidates.rationale: Hall benefit is expressly conditioned on an Agent remaining in Q30; Maker departure is explicitly tested by Q12. Combining Kwisatz Haderach with these facts is not new coverage.

rejected_candidates.candidate: An acquired top-deck card drawn during Reveal, or trashing a newly acquired discard card
rejected_candidates.rationale: Q36/Q54 and Q16/Q66 already specify the destinations, immediate Reveal draw, acquisition interleaving and trash-eligible zones. These are recombinations.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Bindu Suspension consumes a first-player turn while House Hagal acts afterward
rejected_candidates.rationale: Both rules are already required by Q38 and Q18/Q59, and no source states an additional Bindu-specific Rival exception. It is a direct combination.

rejected_candidates.candidate: A different initial combat-marker position, closest garrison, Mentat orientation, or exact physical token inventory
rejected_candidates.rationale: Presentation/component placement details do not add a consequential play branch under the novelty standard. Starting usable forces and scoring are already tested.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Choose versus randomly select a Leader; first-game complexity recommendation and same-House thematic advice
rejected_candidates.rationale: The source permits ordinary Leader selection and gives recommendations; these do not introduce an untested consequential rule/outcome interaction. They are not restrictions requiring new benchmark coverage.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Require saying all five phase names as one answer
rejected_candidates.rationale: The procedural phase operations and their sequencing are already distributed across Q21/Q68/Q10/Q12/Q13. Listing the names together is a mechanical restatement, absent a new timing exception.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Explicitly announce strength aloud before setting its visible marker
rejected_candidates.rationale: Q09 already requires the strength and track representation. The communication wording adds no distinct legal outcome or timing exception.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Uprising Guild Envoy, spies, Shield Wall, contracts, modern Leaders; expansion tech/grafting/dreadnoughts; solo Rival difficulty/VP/Expert deployment
rejected_candidates.rationale: Outside the specified original multiplayer base scope. Shared FAQ headings were read but those subentries were not imported.

limits: Coverage is assessed against the supplied authoritative rulebook and base-game FAQ passages. This review does not assert coverage of every physical card text not reproduced in those sources.
